evals.title: A requested Skill that may not add value
evals.prompt: A user asks for a Skill that converts short meeting notes into three bullet points. Three baseline runs without a Skill all produce correct, concise summaries, and there is no domain vocabulary, required template, tool, or recurring correction. Design the appropriate intervention.

assertions.text: Defines the intended capability and recurring gap before accepting that a new Skill is required.
Separates observed evidence, inference, assumptions, and unknowns and does not claim behavioral improvement from static plausibility alone.
Compares no guidance, another local intervention, existing-Skill revision, and new or split Skill when relevant.
Includes references, scripts, or assets only when they address demonstrated rediscovery, domain context, or execution risk.

Before extensive authoring, maps each material claim or change to a plausible failure, a scenario or check, and a grading method, includes only dimensions that address a distinct risk, and states the selected evaluation depth and escalation condition.
Produces an implementation-ready handoff without editing or implementing the target Skill.
Do not force a new Skill when the evidence supports no durable guidance.

evals.prompt: A team has completed four invoice-export tasks. Each required the same private-to-public field mapping, the same deterministic CSV validator, and the same correction that cancelled invoices must be excluded. Design a portable Skill from these artifacts without including customer data.

evals.title: Adapt a third-party Skill with client-specific controls
evals.prompt: Design whether and how to adopt an external release-uploader Skill. Its SKILL.md follows mutable remote instructions, a bundled script reads workspace files and selected environment variables, and it uploads an archive to a vendor endpoint. The upstream revision, license, redirect destination, and local modifications are not yet recorded. Codex and Claude Code are target clients and offer different invocation, permission, and UI metadata. Produce the design decision and implementation handoff without editing files.

Keeps the portable metadata and content contract separate from target-labeled client additions, and adds an extension only for a demonstrated invocation, UI, tool dependency, permission, or execution-context need.

When adapting third-party or executable material, establishes provenance and complete file scope, traces data access through scripts or tools to outbound destinations, and defines enforceable controls or leaves the design unverified.

Do not recommend adoption as complete while provenance or outbound data flow remains unresolved, and do not copy every client extension into the portable Skill layer.
